Same Tree and Subtree of Another Tree
isSameTree is O(n). isSubtree tries every node as a starting point: O(m·n) worst case. An O(m + n) alternative serialises both trees (with null markers) and does a substring search such as KMP.
Symmetric Tree (mirror of itself)
Compare outer with outer and inner with inner. O(n) time, O(h) stack. Iteratively, push pairs (a.left, b.right) and (a.right, b.left) onto a queue.
Path Sum II: all root-to-leaf paths with a given sum

DFS with a shared path list plus backtracking; copy the path only when a valid leaf is reached. O(n²) worst case because of copying. Path Sum I returns a boolean; Path Sum III (any downward path) uses a prefix-sum HashMap like Subarray Sum Equals K.
Construct Binary Tree from Preorder and Inorder Traversal

The next preorder value is always the current root; its position in inorder splits left and right subtrees. The index map makes each lookup O(1), so the whole build is O(n). Assumes unique values. Inorder alone cannot identify a tree; you need it plus preorder or postorder.
Binary Tree Maximum Path Sum

The same "return one thing, update a global with another" pattern as Diameter. The answer may pass through any node and contain both children, but only one branch can be passed up. O(n) time, O(h) space.
Serialize and Deserialize a Binary Tree

Preorder with null markers is unambiguous, so one traversal is enough to rebuild the tree. O(n) both ways. A BFS (level-order) format like LeetCode's also works. For a BST you can skip the null markers and rebuild using value bounds.
Delete a Node in a BST

Three cases: a leaf is removed, a node with one child is replaced by that child, and a node with two children copies its inorder successor (smallest in the right subtree) and deletes that instead. O(h): O(log n) balanced, O(n) skewed. Java's TreeMap is a red-black tree, which keeps h = O(log n).
DFS (pre / in / post order) vs BFS for tree problems

| Preorder | Inorder | Postorder | BFS (level order)
Visits node | Before children | Between children | After children | Level by level
Good for | Copy / serialize, pass info down | BST in sorted order | Height, diameter, delete tree | Min depth, right side view, per-level work
Extra space | O(h) | O(h) | O(h) | O(w), widest level
Structure | Recursion or stack | Recursion or stack | Recursion or stack | Queue
Rule of thumb: anything "per level" or "closest to the root" → BFS. Children's results needed first → postorder. Sorted BST values → inorder. h is log n for a balanced tree but n for a skewed one.
Top-down (pass values down) vs bottom-up (return values up) recursion

| Top-down | Bottom-up
Information flow | Parameters from parent to child | Return values from child to parent
Typical state | depth, (min, max) bounds, running path sum | height, subtree sum, "is balanced"
Examples | Validate BST, Path Sum, max depth with a depth param | Diameter, Balanced Tree, Max Path Sum
Global answer | Updated at the leaves | Updated at every node, return a different value
Interview tip: when the answer at a node depends on both subtrees, use bottom-up and notice that what you return to the parent is often not the final answer.
Plain BST vs balanced BST (TreeMap) vs heap vs HashMap

| Plain BST | Balanced BST (TreeMap, red-black) | Binary heap | HashMap
Search | O(h), O(n) worst | O(log n) | O(n) | O(1) average
Insert / delete | O(h) | O(log n) | O(log n) | O(1) average
Min / max | O(h) | O(log n) | O(1) for one of them | O(n)
Sorted iteration, floor / ceiling | Yes | Yes | No | No
Shape guarantee | None (sorted inserts make a list) | Height ≤ 2 log(n + 1) | Complete tree | N/A
Rule of thumb: need order queries → TreeMap; need only the top element → PriorityQueue; need only membership → HashMap. Write a plain BST only when the question asks for it.
Inorder traversal: recursive vs iterative stack vs Morris

| Recursive | Iterative with stack | Morris
Time | O(n) | O(n) | O(n)
Extra space | O(h) call stack | O(h) explicit stack | O(1)
Modifies tree | No | No | Temporarily (threads to the inorder predecessor), then restores
Can stop early (Kth Smallest) | Needs a flag | Easy: break out of the loop | Must still restore links
Interview tip: the iterative version is the one most often asked. Mention Morris only if O(1) extra space is required.
